reading.title: Mayor of Maple Street Market
reading.purpose: Join a class that runs a pretend town and learns how trade, taxes, and votes work.
paras: At Maple Street School, Ms. Chen's class ran a pretend town for a week. Each student made something to sell, and the class economy buzzed with trades. Kiran folded paper cranes, but he had only six, so the supply was small. Everyone wanted one, and the demand was so high that the price rose from two tickets to five.

On Tuesday, the class made a rule. Every sale would carry a tax, a small amount of tickets that paid for shared things like the class party. Some students grumbled that the tax was a burden, a heavy cost to carry. Mei reminded them that the party was for everyone.

Next, the class would elect a mayor to lead the town meeting. Two candidates stepped forward, Omar and Priya. Omar promised longer market hours, and Priya promised a safer line for shoppers. Each student received a ballot, a paper for a secret vote, and dropped it into a shoebox after marking it.

Priya won by three votes. Omar shook her hand, and the new mayor called a meeting of the lawmakers, the five students who could change the town rules. "We cannot make a rule alone," she said. "Let us vote on each idea." They agreed not to burden any shopper with new fees.
At the end of the week, the class counted its tickets. The party was paid for, and Kiran asked for a new job: folding twice as many cranes.

choices: a prize given to the student who sells the most
a payment that covers things everyone shares
the price a shopper pays to buy one paper crane
a rule about how many tickets a student may keep
qs.why: The text calls the tax tickets "that paid for shared things like the class party."

qs.q: Which sentence shows how the students voted?
choices: Each student received a ballot, a paper for a secret vote, and dropped it into a shoebox after marking it.
Omar promised longer market hours, and Priya promised a safer line for shoppers.
Two candidates stepped forward, Omar and Priya.
On Tuesday, the class made a rule.
qs.why: This sentence describes the voting itself: a secret ballot marked and dropped in a box.

ev.text: Each student received a ballot, a paper for a secret vote, and dropped it into a shoebox after marking it.

qs.q: Why did the price of Kiran's cranes rise?
choices: The class tax had just been added to every sale that day.
Kiran folded the cranes with more expensive paper from a store.
Ms. Chen told Kiran to ask for more tickets for each crane.
Few cranes were available, and many students wanted one.
qs.why: Kiran had only six cranes (a small supply) and everyone wanted one (high demand), so the price went up.

qs.q: What is the best summary of this story?
choices: A teacher chooses a mayor for the class without holding a vote.
A student wins a contest for folding the most paper cranes in a week.
A class learns how trade, taxes, and votes work in a pretend town.
A school closes its market because the students cannot agree.
qs.why: Each paragraph shows part of the pretend town: trade, a tax, an election, and lawmakers.

clues.text: a small amount of tickets that paid for shared things
a paper for a secret vote
